newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares fall in late IBIS on lower dollar.
newsitem.headline: German shares fall in late IBIS on lower dollar.

text.p: A weaker U.S. dollar saw Germany's DAX index fall nearly one percent in late IBIS DAX trade on Tuesday, while an unsettled Wall Street did little to help boost sentiment later on.

The IBIS DAX index, which measures electronic trade on 30 German stocks, ended at 3,230.83 points, down 29.47 points or 0.90 percent. Earlier the DAX index ended bourse trade at 3,276.16 points, a record closing high.
"Any time the dollar engages in any kind of consolidatory behaviour whatsoever, the market slows up," said one trader.
The dollar was trading at 1.68 marks at the end of IBIS DAX trade, well off the 1.70 marks it traded at earlier on.
"Aside from the dollar, there could be a lot of artificial goings on ahead of this Friday's options expiry, as people try to get into the best position before then," said a trader.

The Dow Jones passed an important threshold at 7,000 points earlier on in dealings on Tuesday, which had it had done on Friday before closing below that level, but soon began to consolidate and then to fall marginally.

Germany's largest commercial bank, Deutsche Bank AG was the volume leader in afternoon trade and it ended the day up 70 pfennigs at 87.80 marks after reporting 1996 group operating profit after risk provisions of 5.8 billion marks.

The banking sector generally benefited from the news, but gains were limited as the market fell in late trade. Dresdner Bank AG ended the day unchanged at 53.90 marks, while Commerzbank ended 40 pfennigs lower at 43 marks.
Construction stock Holzmann AG traded strongly ahead in bourse trade after it said its financial situation had improved and it aimed to restore loss-making operations to profit by next year.
Holzmann shares ended bourse up eight marks at 459 marks, but ended IBIS trade unchanged.

Carmaker Volkswagen AG shares fell sharply to end IBIS trade down 12 marks at 798 marks after a statement that production would be cut due to the Spanish trucker strike interrupting shipments from parts suppliers.

Further pressure came on the stock after VW said it has asked German prosecutors to investigate allegations of purchasing department officials demanding and accepting bribes from suppliers to be given contracts.
